probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Halden® Pricing Changelog Help Blog About Overview Buy Halden App Store Google Play © 2026 Halden® 2 min read September 2, 2026 Why a missed day is only a gap Strict streaks make people quit. A record with room for bad days keeps them coming back. By Elias Berg When we looked at why people stopped using the first version of Halden, the answer was nearly always the same. They had a long run of done days, missed one, watched the counter drop to zero and never opened the app again. A streak is a lovely thing while it lasts. The problem is what it says on the day it breaks: everything you did before no longer counts. For an app about doing one thing a day, that is exactly the wrong message. What we changed Halden no longer counts streaks. It keeps a record instead: a month of squares, one per day, dark when the thing got done and light when it did not. A missed day shows up as a gap and nothing more. The days around it stay dark. The number at the top of the record is how many days got done this month, not how many in a row.
